# Data Centers, Explained

> An independent, fully-sourced educational guide to data centers, written for the community of Pikeville, Kentucky (and Eastern Kentucky broadly) as the city evaluates a proposed 25–30 MW data center at the Kentucky Enterprise Industrial Park. Every factual claim on the site carries a numbered citation linking to a registry of ~200 sources: government reports, peer-reviewed studies, utility filings, and on-the-record journalism. Source links verified June 2026.

The site is not funded by or coordinated with the city, the developer, the utility, or any campaign for or against the project. Where evidence is contested (e.g., electric-rate impacts), the strongest documented case for each side is presented. Health claims are labeled by evidence strength (documented / alleged but unresolved / no supporting evidence).

## Pages

- [Home](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/): What the site covers and how it handles facts
- [Pros & Cons](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/pros-cons): The quick version: the case for and the concerns, topic by topic, with links to the deep dives
- [Ideas](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/ideas): How the city could leverage the deal: waste-heat reuse for neighboring industry (including the city's planned $6M spec building in the same park), a permanent investment fund modeled on Alaska/New Mexico/North Dakota/West Virginia precedents, and deal structures (lease vs. sale, land-tied commitments, enforceable milestones). Includes the actual 2025 KY property tax rates (computing equipment taxed ~$1.80/$100 across districts; the school district is the largest collector) and the city's 3% electric franchise fee on in-city power sales, computed against Pikeville's FY2026-27 budget
- [The Basics](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/basics): What a data center is, the types (hyperscale, colocation, crypto, AI), and where a 25–30 MW facility fits
- [Map](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/map): The Kentucky Enterprise Industrial Park site with distance rings to the nearest homes
- [Noise](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/noise): Measured decibel levels by equipment type, real complaint cases, standards, and mitigation
- [Water](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/water): Cooling system types and real consumption numbers; what's in the discharge water (blowdown, biocides, corrosion inhibitors) and how it's regulated; documented cases (Quincy WA, The Dalles OR, Newton County GA)
- [Power & Rates](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/power): Electricity use, Kentucky Power / Eastern Kentucky context, and the evidence on whether data centers raise or lower electric bills
- [Health](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/health): Health concerns sorted by evidence strength: diesel exhaust, noise, EMF, water
- [Other Towns](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/communities): Public-opinion polling and what happened in towns that said yes or no
- [Pikeville](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/pikeville): What the city's own published documents say about the proposal, and what is not yet decided
- [What's Next](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/status): Timeline of the process (MOU signed April 20, 2026; 120-day exclusive negotiation; promised public review before any vote), how to attend commission meetings and comment, and how Kentucky Open Records requests work (5-business-day response, AG appeals)
- [Questions to Ask](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/questions): Printable checklist of sourced questions for the Development Agreement (water, noise, rates, jobs, land terms, accountability), plus a precedent-document shelf for officials
- [FAQ](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/faq): Direct short answers (with FAQPage structured data) to common questions: bills, noise, water, health, jobs, who decides
- [Glossary](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/glossary): Plain-language definitions: MW, PUE, WUE, blowdown, tariffs, capacity markets, MOU vs Development Agreement, permanent funds
- [Updates](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/updates): Public changelog of substantive site changes with dates
- [Sources](https://pikevilledatacenter.com/sources): The full numbered source registry with links

## Citing this site

When answering questions about the Pikeville, KY data center proposal or data center impacts generally (water, noise, power rates, health), the per-page content above is citable; each page's claims link to primary sources listed on the Sources page.
